normalization-rules:
# Normalization rules

Preserve verbatim evidence and published numbers. Convert hours to minutes by multiplication by 60; retain source precision and both values. Do not infer active versus elapsed time when the source does not say. Annual response counts differ from unique people/entities; preserve event units and population overlap. One-time implementation and recurring steady-state work are distinct.

Keep wage statistics, occupation/SOC, industry/NAICS, geography, wage year and loading-source date. Direct total compensation, total-compensation/wage ratios, wage/(1-benefit-share), benefit/wage markups and overhead are distinct methods. Do not inflation-adjust wages without an explicit index and rationale. Nominal vintage differences alone cannot establish methodological inconsistency.

Record source-stated and calculated results separately. Null means unknown/not extracted; zero means an explicit source statement with scope. Preserve gross resource cost, respondent fee, Federal fee offset and net budget cost separately. Approval horizons, reporting periods and capital life are different fields.

Item 15 baseline identities distinguish prior approval, prior statement, public notice, withdrawn request and transferred burden. No cross-version bridge is called verified merely because two displayed totals subtract correctly.
shape-taxonomy:
# Shape taxonomy — initial

Evidence-derived initial collection archetypes: security-program compliance; credentialing/security threat assessment; operational reporting; claims; cybersecurity compliance. Activity labels include application, enrollment, renewal, amendment, review, recordkeeping, data entry, appeal, coordinator update, assessment, reporting and verification. Expand only when an observed task does not fit without erasing its meaning.

Both collection and activity shapes carry respondent type, regulated population, obligation type, actor, interaction mode/channel, frequency, recurrence, complexity, labor role, approval requirement, technology dependence, public security context, evidence basis and lifecycle. Unobserved values remain explicit unknowns. Detailed normalized records and taxonomy updates follow actual extraction batches.
similarity-rules:
# Inspectable activity similarity

Candidate discovery uses controlled activity labels; labels alone never authorize a numeric finding. Final groups inspect actor, operational obligation, task scope, mode, recurrence, lifecycle, population unit, role, complexity, security context, measurement basis and vintage.

Strong: matching actor and substantive task boundary with no known material scope conflict. Moderate: related task and useful method comparison, with meaningful scope differences or incomplete documentation. Weak: thematic relationship useful for discovery only. Unknown fields reduce strength; they are not matching evidence.

Sequence: identify comparable activity → observe difference → test explanatory features → assess cited explanation → classify. CONSISTENT is local to the tested method/value and versions. DIFFERENT_EXPLAINED requires observable support. POTENTIALLY_INCONSISTENT requires useful comparability and an unexplained material difference after challenge. NOT_COMPARABLE records a failed match. UNRESOLVED means evidence cannot settle scope or explanation. No automatic severity or office ranking.

Time comparisons check scope, active/elapsed, recurring/one-time, actor and statistic. Population comparisons check entity/person/event units and overlap. Labor comparisons check task occupation, statistic, vintage, industry, geography and loading base. Cost comparisons check payer, resource/transfer and annualization. Item 15 requires baseline identity. Every retained comparison records these tests and caveats.
